title: 3.3.14 Lab: Write a Function That Returns a New Array
description: Write a function that builds and returns a new array of transformed values (for example, each number doubled with result.push(n * 2), as in 3.3.12), proving the original is untouched. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write a function with an array parameter
steps.instructions: Write a function declaration (e.g. doubled or bigger) that takes an array parameter.

steps.title: Build a new array inside it
steps.instructions: Create a new empty array inside the function and use a for...of loop to push each transformed value in.

steps.title: Return the new array
steps.instructions: After the loop, return the new array.

steps.title: Call it and log both arrays
steps.instructions: Call the function with a sample array and console.log both the result and the original array to show the original is untouched.

requirements.title: function with an array parameter that is not mutated
requirements.description: Code declares a function whose array parameter is never changed inside it (no push, pop, shift, unshift, splice, sort, reverse, fill or index assignment on it). Help: 3.3.12 (Arrays and Functions)

requirements.title: for loop present
requirements.description: Code uses a for or for...of loop. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays (for / for…of))

requirements.title: function returns the new array
requirements.description: A return inside the function hands back the new array. Help: 3.3.12 (Arrays and Functions)

requirements.title: the new array differs from the input
requirements.description: A pushed value is changed (arithmetic or a call) or only pushed when an if says so, so the result is not a plain copy. Help: 3.3.12 (Arrays and Functions)

requirements.title: both arrays are logged
requirements.description: console.log is called at least twice: once for the returned array and once for the original. Help: 3.3.12 (Arrays and Functions)
